articles.title: McKenna helps Maple Leafs beat Islanders to end winless streak
articles.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs spotted the New York Islanders a 2-0 lead on Monday and it appeared as if the Canadian visitors were on their way to a 10th straight loss. But Dakota Joshua, Chris Tanev, Gavin McKenna and Easton Cowan with an empty-netter, scored four unanswered goals for the Leafs, who beat the Islanders […]

articles.title: Police wouldn’t have arrested Francique if he stayed home, detective tells inquest
articles.summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a Black man who was shot by police in Mississauga, Ont., heard Monday that officers did not necessarily plan to arrest him that night nearly seven years ago. Peel regional police Det. Mani Sharifi said that changed when officers surveilling Jamal Francique saw him breaching his bail conditions […]

articles.title: 2 injured in Mississauga crash involving Peel police cruiser
articles.summary: A Peel Regional Police Service cruiser was involved in a two-vehicle collision in Mississauga Monday evening. The crash happened around 7:40 p.m. on Dixie Road south of Rathburn Road. Police say two people were transported to hospital with non-life threatening injuries. It is not yet clear whether any officers were transported to the hospital. Investigators […]

articles.title: Steven Del Duca uses ‘strong mayor’ powers to replace York Region top civil servant
articles.summary: York Region’s chief administrative officer is departing from her position, according to freshly appointed York Region Chair Steven Del Duca. Less than two weeks after being appointed regional chair by the Ford government, Del Duca has invoked his “strong mayor” powers to replace CAO Erin Mahoney. However, Del Duca tells CityNews the departure was reached […]

articles.title: Mississauga family spent just over $1,000 to power home and two electric cars in 2025
articles.summary: MISSISSAUGA, Ont. — With heating costs expected to peak during Canada’s coldest months, one Mississauga family says it managed to cover its home and transportation energy costs for approximately $1,100 in 2025. Harminder Dhillon and Jyoti Grewal have gone to considerable lengths to reduce their reliance on conventional energy sources. They have installed rooftop solar […]

articles.title: Brampton mayor sees 'crack of cautious optimism' as Stellantis weighs plant sale
articles.summary: Stellantis officials met with federal, provincial and union representatives last week who touted major movements in discussions. Could a change in emissions standards be the key to reopening the plant? Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown joins Power & Politics to discuss the latest.

articles.summary: A coroner's inquest into the death of a Black man who was shot by police in Mississauga, Ont., heard Monday that officers did not necessarily plan to arrest him that night nearly seven years ago.

articles.title: City of Mississauga to implement hiring restrictions effective immediately
articles.summary: One week into the term of Mississauga's new mayor and hiring restrictions are going into effect at the city. It comes after staff were directed by Mayor Alvin Tedjo to freeze property taxes for the 2027 and 2028 budgets.

articles.title: Motorcyclist seriously injured after being hit by vehicle in Scarborough
articles.summary: Toronto police say a male motorcyclist has been injured in a Scarborough collision Monday afternoon. Emergency crews were called to Birchmount Road and Bonis Avenue just before 3:15 p.m. for reports of a crash. When they arrived on scene, police found a male motorcyclist who they say was injured after being struck by a vehicle. […]

articles.title: Peel, Halton police launch annual Miracle on Main Street campaign ahead of holiday season
articles.summary: Police in Peel and Halton regions launched their annual Miracle on Main Street campaign Monday, which seeks to provide toy, gift card and essential item donations for families in need.

articles.title: Construction begins in Toronto's west end as city prepares for months-long disruption
articles.summary: Work has officially begun to replace and improve infrastructure on sections of King Street W. in downtown Toronto. The work is scheduled to continue for around 10 months, ending in fall of 2027.

articles.title: Toronto's top bureaucrat leaving city hall, Chow uses 'strong mayor' powers to appoint interim replacement
articles.summary: Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow has signed off on an overhaul of some of Toronto’s top bureaucratic roles, including city manager, as part of a restructuring of the city's internal operations.

articles.title: Toronto police arrest man wanted for Etobicoke homicide
articles.summary: Toronto police say they have arrested a man in connection with a fatal Etobicoke shooting this month.

articles.title: Brampton hackathon asks students to use AI to fix local businesses' issues
articles.summary: The Brampton Venture Zone held its first student hackathon over the weekend. It's the first part of a program that will see students get the opportunity to work with businesses, helping companies use artificial intelligence to solve common problems.

articles.title: 122nd Original Santa Claus Parade brings holiday cheer to downtown Toronto
articles.summary: Crowds gathered downtown Sunday for Toronto’s 122nd Original Santa Claus Parade, featuring 23 floats and more than 1,500 marchers. The parade also saw live performances along the route, with Santa and Mrs. Claus making their return to the city.

articles.title: Man, 61, dies after being struck by vehicle in Scarborough: police
articles.summary: A 61-year-old man has died after he was struck by a vehicle in Scarborough Saturday, Toronto police say.

articles.title: 2 teens dead, 1 injured after shooting at Scarborough gas station: police
articles.summary: Two 16-year-old boys died following a shooting at a Scarborough gas station early Sunday that left a third teen with serious gunshot wounds, according to Toronto police.

articles.title: Black creatives at Brampton conference vow to transform future of arts industry
articles.summary: A group of Black creatives met in Brampton over the weekend to re-envision how they can strengthen the arts sector for Black artists.

articles.title: In clay, these artists model the pain and beauty of diaspora
articles.summary: The Gardiner Museum’s After the Island asks four Caribbean Canadian artists what it means to have roots in two lands. The exhibition — featuring ceramics and more — includes the work of PJ Anderson, Manuel Mathieu, Sharon Norwood and Eddy Firmin.
